sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
EMA Partners India Limited; NSE Emerge, SM series, EMAPARTNER, ISIN INE0ZOL01023. The January 2025 IPO did not create the operating business, founded in 2003. Information cutoff: 20 October 2026; reconstruction/access: 21 October. Only cutoff-eligible information enters the conclusions. NSE final close on 19 October was ₹80, not an executable bid. 20 October was the Dussehra market holiday. Actual post-buyback shares: 22,521,426; market capitalization: ₹180.171408 crore. [S1,S8,S12,S13,S24]

Scope: consolidated Indian GAAP Accounting Standards, not Ind AS. The annual report explicitly identifies the SME exemption. Operating leases are expensed under AS19. March 2026 accounts exclude the July Taggd acquisition; the group ultimately owns 100% of Taggd, so its omitted economics cannot be treated as immaterial or as a minority investment. [S1,S7]

Analytical horizon: five years, nominal INR. Equity hurdle: 15% before personal taxes, with 12% and 18% sensitivities. A judgmental 12–16% nominal capital-cost range is used only to interpret legacy incremental returns, not as an observed issuer WACC. Liquidity reference: ₹5 lakh at 2%, 5% and 10% participation; 5% is primary.

G1 Integrity: Clear within reviewed evidence. G2 Reliability: Conditional. G3 Funding: Hold, unresolved. G4 Tradability: Conditional. No numerical override is triggered by merely missing evidence. Data confidence is high on audited legacy financials and dated primary quote, medium on governance, repeat business and organic growth, and low on target economics and actual combined valuation. Forecast uncertainty is high. The financial information gap is not an allegation of false accounting. [S1,S2,S5,S6,S7,S8,S12,S20–S24]

Liquidity implementation: 60-session mean/median actual turnover ₹10.11270/8.14975 lakh; 20-session ₹12.73355/9.40800 lakh. Counting three inferred no-print dates, continuous median-based ₹5 lakh exit estimates at 2%/5%/10% are 30.68/12.27/6.14 sessions (20-session sensitivity 26.57/10.63/5.31). Exact ₹5 lakh is 6.25 lots and not executable in whole lots: six lots cost ₹4.8 lakh and seven ₹5.6 lakh before costs. Starting L3 is reduced to final L1 for integer-lot constraints. [S12,S13,S24]

Whole-lot capacity over 60 sessions at 2%/5%/10%: eligible days 1/10/31, zero-capacity days 59/50/29, total lots 1/13/51. Over 20 sessions: eligible days 1/3/13, total lots 1/5/22. At 5%, six/seven-lot exits need 27.69/32.31 sessions at mean observed whole-lot capacity; daily median capacity iszero, so a median-based discrete estimate is not finite. Historical rolling completed paths take median 25/27 sessions but censor 20/21 starts and are not unbiased expected waits. At 2%, the full 60-session window cannot execute either position; at 10%, mean-capacity equivalents are 7.06/8.24 sessions. All assume bids exist and therefore may still overstate executable capacity. [S12,S13,S24]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Nine business factors and four additional IAS factors, all on the framework's fixed integer scale:

GOV: 6/10; confidence medium; evidence E7, E8, E11, E12. Unmodified audit and disclosed RPTs/IPO allocation changes support adequate transparency; promoters did not sell into the buyback. Contrary evidence: loss-making deployments, subsequent large acquisition after a cash return, and missing post-deal economics prevent a stronger stewardship score. Ordinary litigation/RPTs are not evidence of diversion.

MOAT: 6/10; confidence medium; evidence E15, E3. Repeat business of 76.38% and high C-suite concentration evidence trusted relationships and specialized search capability. Contrary evidence: mandates are not annuities, consultants can leave, and global search/RPO competitors can contest accounts; no independently verified structural market-share moat.

REV: 7/10; confidence medium; evidence E2, E18. Five-year 22.2539% CAGR starts at 8; apply−1 for the pandemic-depressed FY21 base, corroborated by only 11.2876% FY22–26 growth. Three-year 20.3303% and H2FY26 recovery are positives, but not a second trajectory bonus. No small-size penalty or forecast/Taggd revenue bonus.

DUR: 6/10; confidence medium; evidence E15, E9, E19. Existing India/Dubai/Singapore relationships and acquired RPO clients create accessible adjacent demand; board advisory adds a plausible service avenue. Contrary evidence: hiring cyclicality, unproven cross-selling/unit economics, and loss-making new units mean headline TAM is not a funded runway.

CAP: NS/10; confidence low; evidence E13, E8, E9. Legacy operating ROIC is strong at 26.96%, but one-year incremental proxy is 4.27% and a ₹96.75 crore completed acquisition changes committed capital materially. Target profitability/acquired working capital/debt and new-unit cohorts are missing. No legacy ROIC substitution for current incremental returns.

CASH: 5/10; confidence medium; evidence E4, E5. Five-year 64.96% and three-year 60.69% reported conversion are mixed; FY26 negative CFO reflects collections and taxes, not capex. Contrary positive: FY24–25 CFO was positive and FY25 collection release helped. A one-year receivable spike is not enough to assert persistent destructive cash realization, so no≤3 override.

BAL: NS/10; confidence low; evidence E6, E8, E10, E12. Audited March debt was just ₹0.591 crore, a positive; however that cash predates buyback/acquisition and includes earmarked/group funds. Missing interim cash generation, target obligations and transferability prevent credible actual post-deal stress coverage. Conditional arithmetic gap is not proven default.

EXEC: 5/10; confidence medium; evidence E12, E18, E19. Taggd closure and completed buyback are delivered milestones, and H2 revenue recovered strongly. Contrary evidence: James Douglas losses, eroded-net-worth subsidiaries and abandoned Decision Dynamics plan; promised new-business profitability remains unverified. Do not score acquisition announcement as integration success.

EARN: 5/10; confidence medium; evidence E2, E3, E12. Recurring operating EBITDA grew 8%FY26 with revenue 18%, and normalized core group profit remains positive. Contrary evidence: ownerPAT belowFY24, dilutedEPS5.29 vs 8.40, investment income/deferred-tax credits and new-vertical losses weaken reported per-share growth quality.

R: NS/10; confidence low; evidence E9, E10, E17. Actual post-acquisition target earnings/claims and unrestricted liquidity are not established; no supported common-equity five-year base IRR. The fully funded no-Taggd counterfactual is not the purchased entity and cannot supply R, even though its base exceeds 15%.

D: NS/10; confidence low; evidence E10, E12, E17. Credible stress links recruitment slowdown, receivable stretch, target losses and restricted liquidity; March debt was low and legacy operations profitable. Actual target claims/funding gap are unknown, so downside severity/recovery cannot be scored from a counterfactual survival case.

P: NS/10; confidence low; evidence E3, E6, E9. 14.64 xFY26 ownerPAT and 20.22 xnormalizedlegacyPAT are only stale-perimeter references; they omit acquired target earnings and cash-yield loss. Current price-implied combined growth cannot be solved without a target earnings/claim bridge. Do not interpret the obsolete net-cash EV as a bargain.

L: 1/10; confidence high; evidence E1, E16, E20, E21. Starting L3 follows the lower of 60-session mean and median actual traded value, giving 12.27 continuous theoretical sessions. Whole-lot execution at 5% is much worse: only 10/60 dates eligible,13 total lots, and 27.69/32.31 mean-capacity sessions for six/seven lots. Apply an explicit two-point lot-size/execution downgrade to final L1. Positive contrary evidence: Active SM, no identified ASM/GSM/ESM measure and improved recent turnover. NSE liquidity cautions and unknown bid depth prevent an orderly-execution uplift.

BQS = 0.20 GOV + 0.20 MOAT + 0.12 REV + 0.10 DUR + 0.12 CAP + 0.10 CASH + 0.08 BAL + 0.08 EXEC. Known contributions are 1.20 + 1.20 + 0.84 + 0.60 + NS + 0.50 + NS + 0.40 = 4.74. Coverage 80%; raw and final NS. Missing-data bounds 4.94–6.74, not a confidence interval or substitute score.

GQS, Growth Quality Score, = 0.40 REV + 0.20 DUR + 0.15 EARN + 0.15 CAP + 0.10 CASH. Contributions: 2.80 + 1.20 + 0.75 + NS + 0.50 = 5.25. Coverage 85%; raw and final NS; missing-data bounds 5.40–6.75.

IAS = 0.25 final BQS + 0.35 R + 0.20 D + 0.10 P + 0.10 L. Only L contributes 0.10. Coverage 10%; raw and final NS; conservative missing-data bounds 1.00–9.10. BQS is not replaced with a midpoint or its known subtotal. All three scores are excluded from ranked lists.

No governance cap: GOV is 6 and G1 does not fail. No funding cap: G3 is unresolved, not an evidenced failure. No growth cap: CASH is 5 and persistent CAP≤3 has not been established. The framework would cap BQS/IAS at 3 after a substantiated governance failure, IAS at 3 after G3 failure, and GQS at 5 for persistent CAP/CASH≤3; those are contingent rules, not current findings.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The original franchise provides retained executive search and leadership advisory, including board and C-suite mandates. James Douglas extends into professional/middle-management search; newer recruitment and digital ventures add different delivery models. Taggd adds enterprise recruitment-process outsourcing. Revenue is earned for search/advisory engagements and recruitment service delivery, not simply for listing jobs online. Mandate milestones, successful delivery, consultant incentives and collections determine cash economics. [S1,S2,S7,S10]

FY26 legacy consolidated revenue was ₹87.364 crore: India ₹60.593 crore and outside India ₹26.771 crore, principally through the Dubai and Singapore operations. The audited headcount was 109; the earnings call's 107 is a different management snapshot, not a reason to overwrite the audited number. The call described 44 search professionals, but current billable headcount, placements per consultant, utilization and realized fees are not independently reconciled. [S1,S11]

People costs of ₹54.378 crore were 62.24% of sales. Other operating costs of ₹18.612 crore, including rent, produced ₹14.374 crore EBITDA before depreciation and finance cost. Gross profit is not meaningfully separately disclosed. Unlike salary pass-through staffing, executive-search fees have high gross economic value per mandate, but a fixed consultant base creates operating leverage when hiring demand slows. [S1]

Taggd's disclosed audited turnover was ₹40.8155/78.1597/93.0208 crore in FY23/FY24/FY25. The presentation's FY26 Taggd ₹108 crore and combined ₹195 crore are management pro-forma revenue, not audited combined FY26 results or an earnings forecast. Target revenue is not free cash flow; target compensation, collections, debt and senior claims remain essential missing inputs. [S7,S10]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The strongest mechanism is accumulated trust with boards and senior executives, specialized consultant networks and the cost of a failed leadership appointment. FY24 repeat-client revenue of 76.38% and repeat-client count of 68.90% support relationship continuity. Repeat means a client billed at least twice, not contracted recurring subscription revenue. Board/C-suite work represented approximately 86.82% of FY24 sales. [S2]

Concentration is material but not a single-client dependency: FY24 top ten customers were 34.47% of revenue and the largest 13.21%. The July 2024 partial period had top-ten concentration of 41.65%; periods are not directly comparable. Customer logos and global-network affiliation do not establish exclusive access, market share or pricing power. Senior consultants can leave, and clients can move mandates without changing a physical production system. No durable independently measured market-share advantage was established. [S2]

Korn Ferry is a larger search/RPO/advisory comparator: its official FY26 release reports fee revenue of USD2.9075 billion, growth of 7%, and adjusted EBITDA margin of 17.1%. Heidrick & Struggles overlaps in executive search and leadership services. TeamLease is an adjacent Indian staffing/HR-services comparator for payroll and collection discipline, not a like-for-like fee-margin or EV/sales comparator because staffing includes salary pass-through economics. These are business-model comparisons, not a fabricated peer-pricing table. Dynamic service pages are used only for taxonomy, not dated market metrics. [S14,S15,S16]

MOAT6 recognizes real relationships while rejecting a monopoly thesis. Current client churn, consultant retention, pricing versus volume, and Taggd client concentration are ND. Management's description of Taggd as a leading homegrown RPO does not supply an independently verified market-share denominator. [S7,S10]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Consolidated revenue, ₹crore: FY21 31.9904; FY22 56.9568; FY23 50.1428; FY24 67.2962; FY25 73.930498; FY26 87.364183. FY21 is the audited comparison in the scanned FY22 annual report; FY22–24 use IPO-restated figures; FY25–26 use annual accounts. Annual rupee additions for FY22–26: +24.9664, −6.8140, +17.1534, +6.634298 and +13.433685. [S1–S4]

CAGR endpoints and periods: FY21–26, five years, 22.2539%; FY23–26, three years, 20.3303%; FY22–26, four years, 11.2876%. Ten-year comparable history was not established, so 10Y CAGR is ND. The five-year window is selected before scoring. REV starts at 8 for 22.25% growth and receives one downward point for the pandemic-depressed FY21 base, corroborated by the weaker post-pandemic four-year trend. No extra small-base penalty and no forecast/acquisition bonus are applied.

Annual growth was −11.96% in FY23, +34.21% in FY24, +9.86% in FY25 and +18.17% in FY26. H1 FY26 revenue was ₹40.528154 crore versus ₹39.164051 crore, +3.48%; H2 was ₹46.836029 crore versus ₹34.766447 crore, +34.72%. The strong second half is useful contrary evidence to a stagnation thesis but does not by itself establish another sustained-trajectory bonus. FY27 H1 results were not located by the cutoff. [S19]

Taggd enters after FY26 and must be separated from future like-for-like growth. Earlier purchases of minority interests did not create wholly new consolidated sales. Smaller entities, translation and service mix complicate precise organic attribution. A comparable price/placements/FX bridge is ND. No seasonal quarter is annualized, and no overlapping TTM is invented.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Accessible demand comes from leadership mandates, professional search, enterprise RPO and board advisory. Shared client access makes cross-selling plausible; it does not prove identical margins or collection economics. The April call attributed about ₹25 crore EBITDA to the mature business and about ₹11 crore EBITDA loss to new verticals, with ₹15 crore expenditure including ₹11 crore employee costs. These are management explanations, not separately audited segment profits. The target of new-business profitability over the following twelve months remains a milestone to test. [S1,S11]

A bottom-up plan needs productive consultants × completed assignments per consultant × realized fee × collection rate. The audited 109 group employees are not a disclosed billable-consultant base. Illustratively, 5% growth in productive capacity and 6.67% growth in revenue per productive unit compound to 12%; 10% and 9.09% compound to 20%. These are transparent arithmetic indices, not verified hiring plans. Employee cost already absorbs 62.24% of revenue, so hiring ahead of mandates can consume cash. [S1]

Legacy operating ROIC of 26.96% is not the return on the completed ₹96.75 crore Taggd investment. The one-year incremental proxy is only 4.27%, and loss-making new units challenge the proposition that every reinvested rupee earns historical core returns. Audited target profit and acquired capital are missing, hence CAP NS and GQS NS at 85% coverage. No persistent-value-destruction cap is asserted without sufficient evidence. [S1,S6,S7]

The five-year legacy counterfactual explicitly funds payroll, capex and working capital, but it cannot prove the combined group's funding. The actual acquisition is irreversible in this analysis. Runway becomes investment-quality only after target retention, unit economics, funding and group cash availability are reconciled. The September STAIR partnership expands potential board services, but no contracted revenue or cash-return milestone was established. [S17]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Founder executives K. Sudarshan and S. Krishnaprakash have long operating experience. FY26 disclosed remuneration totals ₹1.95 crore, about 15.85% of owner PAT. Selectema related-party rent of ₹0.486 crore and security deposit of ₹0.215 crore are disclosed; their existence alone is not evidence of abuse. CFO Manish Dhanuka resigned on 30 June 2025 and Kushal Parmar was appointed on 22 September 2025. Statutory auditor A. P. Sanzgiri's opinion is unmodified; its second five-year reappointment is not an auditor resignation. No auditor-reported fraud or default was identified in FY26. [S1]

The prospectus describes an ex-employee civil claim for ₹79.76 lakh plus interest, and an independent director's separate historical Xerox complaint concerning managerial remuneration. These are disclosed allegations/proceedings, not findings of EMA fraud. Current disposition was not verified. The annual ₹0.76 crore contingency is kept distinct from the older claim; exact identity and outcome are not assumed. Promoters held 65.76% after the buyback and did not tender, a positive alignment observation rather than proof of allocation skill. Latest pledge clearance is ND. [S1,S2,S8]

Dated promises versus delivery:
- January 2025 IPO: leadership, IT, property-debt repayment and inorganic growth. Audited notes show applications and a shareholder-approved budget variation on 27 March 2026, with utilization extended to March 2028. Reallocation was disclosed, not treated as unauthorized diversion.
- April 2026 buyback: ₹7.25 crore, 725,000 shares, completed and extinguished by 22 May.
- June/July Taggd transaction: completed 6 July; exact approved purchase plus subscription ₹96.7505245 crore, rather than the presentation's rounded ₹95 crore.
- April new-business profitability target: not yet verified achieved.
- 24 September WOS merger: scheme submitted for three wholly owned subsidiaries; effectiveness not independently established.
- 29 September STAIR partnership: announced; incremental earnings not verified. [S1,S6–S11,S17,S18]

Contrary allocation evidence is material: Emagine and RecCloud had eroded net worth; Decision Dynamics' business plan was abandoned; FY26 James Douglas India and Dubai lost ₹5.625 crore and ₹4.082 crore. These lower GOV/EXEC without inventing malfeasance. GOV6 and G1 Clear mean adequate, not exemplary, stewardship within the reviewed evidence. [S1]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
All amounts below are ₹crore. FY22–24 are IPO-restated consolidated accounts; FY25–26 are annual consolidated accounts. Normalized PAT is before NCI, excludes all other income and uses a 25% analyst tax rate. It is not reported owner EPS.

FY23 | 50.143 | 4.078 | 3.200 | 2.936 / 3.071 | 2.258 | 2.721 | 0.366 | 2.355
FY24 | 67.296 | 16.486 | 15.329 | 14.617 / 14.273 | 11.357 | 11.924 | 11.770 | 0.154

[S1,S2,S4]

FY26 normalization: reported PAT 12.305010 − other income 3.217492 + reported tax 2.793369 − normalized core tax 2.970222 = 8.910665. Other income includes deposit interest ₹2.959 crore and a net investment loss ₹0.528 crore; the ₹1.998 crore deferred-tax credit is not cash profit. Net DTA ₹1.482 crore includes ₹1.975 crore from losses. No automatic future tax benefit is valued. Diluted EPS for FY22–26 is ₹6.62, ₹1.81, ₹8.40, ₹6.73 and ₹5.29, on each period's weighted basis. FY26 weighted shares were 23.246426 million versus 22.521426 million current issued shares. Audited diluted EPS does not mean economically outstanding options are irrelevant. [S1,S2]

Five-year CFO/PAT = 34.936814 / 53.778892 = 64.9638%; three-year conversion is 60.6913%. These are ratios of sums using group PAT before NCI, not averages of annual ratios or mismatched owner PAT. Earlier cash-flow statements include NCI-labelled movements within CFO; excluding those classification items raises five-year conversion to about 68.19%, still mixed. FY26 pre-working-capital operating cash ₹18.213 crore fell to ₹6.135 crore after operating movements; ₹6.795 crore cash taxes produced negative CFO. Receivables absorbed ₹11.875 crore. Capex explains weak FCF, not weak CFO. Five-year FCF proxy totals ₹16.415 crore; FY26 FCF proxy is −₹3.873 crore. [S1,S2,S4]

Closing receivables rose 93.2% to ₹25.419 crore against 18.17% sales growth. Closing-balance days rose from 64.95 to 106.20; average-balance days were 78.82 and 80.58, using total revenue as proxy for credit revenue. Ageing includes ₹2.443 crore at 6–12 months and ₹0.092 crore at 1–2 years, measured from transaction date, not contractual due date. Zero closing allowance after a ₹0.388 crore reversal requires collection verification, not a fraud allegation. Contract assets are not separately quantified; inventory is not a material reported service-business bucket. Payable days/CCC are not manufactured with an unsuitable staff-cost denominator. [S1]

Gross debt for FY22–26: ₹3.896, ₹0.560, ₹7.580, ₹1.337 and ₹0.591 crore. Gross treasury: ₹26.352, ₹23.011, ₹30.873, ₹108.671 and ₹108.367 crore. Equity: ₹39.441, ₹39.968, ₹54.016, ₹137.501 and ₹153.714 crore. The IPO explains much of the equity/treasury jump. Historical gross treasury is not unrestricted current cash. FY24 cash capex of ₹11.770 crore includes office investment; FY25 non-cash transfers from CWIP must not be substituted for cash capex. Maintenance versus growth capex is ND. [S1,S2,S4]

FY26 operating IC = equity 153.713907 + debt 0.590927 − treasury 108.366540 − DTA1.481558 − prepaid tax 4.886074 − interest receivable 0.275528 + interest payable 0.003639 = 39.298773. It matches fixed/intangible/CWIP20.448595 + ONWC18.850178, including operating staff advances, deposits and goodwill. FY25 IC is 27.217243. sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
Actual post-Taggd common-equity valuation: NS. The completed acquisition cannot be cancelled to make the current shareholder's cash bridge work. A defensible combined five-year base return needs target operating profit, cash conversion, acquired working capital, debt/senior claims, acquisition accounting and a current unrestricted-cash reconciliation. None is assumed zero. No actual target price or entry range is issued. [S6,S7,S10]

Current market cap divided by FY26 reported legacy owner PAT is 14.64 x; divided by normalized legacy group PAT it is 20.22 x. ₹80 divided by the old weighted EPS₹5.29 gives 15.12 x because its share denominator differs. These are stale-perimeter cross-checks, not combined forward P/E. Current EV/EBITDA and P/B cannot be responsibly calculated by subtracting March cash from October market cap. FY26 FCF yield is negative and not an attractive owner-cash-yield argument. [S1,S8,S12]

ACTUAL FUNDING, CONDITIONAL BRIDGE. Starting residual−₹12.4086495 crore is the dated March-to-disclosed-payments arithmetic in section 9, not current cash. Add U, interim legacy net cash movements after tax/capex and operating liabilities, plus releases of IPO restrictions only where eligible spending is already included in those cash movements. Add T, target unrestricted liquidity net of due senior/settlement claims, excluding the already counted phantom obligation. Subtract K, transaction costs, taxes/remittance friction and other cash claims not already included. Existing financing raised/repaid after March is a separate F reconciliation; no loan is assumed approved. For stress illustration only, U=0/10/20, T=−10/0/10 and K=0.25 produce residuals from−22.659 to+17.341 crore. With a hypothetical ₹3 crore minimum buffer, new financing need ranges ₹25.659 crore tozero. U10/T0 implies ₹5.659 crore need; U10/T10 impliesnone. These are sensitivities, not measured balances or forecasts. Double-counting eligible spending in U and an unreduced earmark would be wrong. The ₹0.25 crore cost placeholder is not a claim about actual buyback/acquisition taxes or fees. [S1,S5–S8]

SEPARATE LEGACY-ONLY COUNTERFACTUAL, NOT ACTUAL EMA. To preserve useful operating analysis, the following five-year model asks what the audited legacy business could support had Taggd never been acquired. This counterfactual excludes both the target and its ₹96.75 crore purchase; it is not the actual bear/base/bull valuation, not evidence of actual survival, and never supplies R, D or P. It resets the audited March operating base into five hypothetical annual periods ending 19 October 2031; no missing FY27 period is represented as observed.

Opening unrestricted cash ₹76.543909 crore = March gross treasury 108.366540 − all IPO restrictions 22.968065 − completed buyback 7.25 − assumed costs 0.25 − legacy debt 0.590927 − interest payable 0.003639 − conservative settlement of disclosed contingency 0.76. This assumes the historical group treasury can be realized and transferred at carrying value in this counterfactual only. No prepaid-tax asset/DTA recovery is added. Restricted cash starts ₹22.968065 crore. First-year release ₹9.595881 and second-year release ₹7.178784 cover eligible payroll/IT/general costs already charged through operating cash/capex; release is a reclassification, not new income. Remaining acquisition earmark ₹6.1934 is excluded from terminal equity. [S1,S5,S8]

Cash EBITDA assumptions include cash salaries, incentives and AS19 rent, but precede any future noncash option-accounting charge; identified equity-option claims are handled through terminal dilution rather than counted twice as cash compensation. D&A is 2.8% of revenue; cash tax 25% of positive EBIT, with no loss-credit benefit or treasury interest income. Receivables equal revenue×DSO/365. Other operating assets and operating liabilities scale at audited FY26/revenue ratios, starting from ₹9.694459 crore and ₹16.263144 crore. Opening ONWC is ₹18.850178 crore. CFO=cash EBITDA−cash tax−ΔONWC; FCF=CFO−cash capex. Operating liabilities settle/reaccrue within ΔONWC, not a second equity deduction. No dividends, new debt or rescue equity are assumed. Capex includes the ₹0.185 crore commitment once. Unknown additional claims, deterioration of retention loans, cash-transfer friction and fresh acquisitions would invalidate this diagnostic.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
Strongest counterargument to the thesis: the mature search franchise may subsidize less productive recruitment ventures while the acquisition consumes the treasury that previously insulated shareholders. A hiring slowdown reduces mandates, expensive consultants remain, collection periods stretch, and target retention/integration costs arrive before synergies. These risks are correlated, not three independent small setbacks. FY26 receivable growth and new-unit losses are observed warning signals. [S1,S11]

Actual impairment risk: High, with low confidence in severity, not a declaration of insolvency. If cash is trapped/earmarked and acquired liabilities or loss funding are material, common shareholders bear dilution, emergency-debt costs, foregone growth spending or residual-value loss. If target economics are strong, receivables collect and unrestricted liquidity is sufficient, the same acquisition could diversify demand and improve scale. Both possibilities remain open. [S1,S6,S7]

The actual funding grid in section 10 quantifies conditional cash needs without inventing target balances. For illustration, a ₹15.659 crore residual financing requirement would issue roughly 1.957 million shares at ₹80 before issue costs,8.69% of current shares; at a ₹60 stress price it would require 2.610 million,11.59%. This is hypothetical rescue dilution, not an announced issuance. Debt financing would instead require verified facilities, covenants and service capacity. The existing 1.7035 million option claims are separate, and option proceeds are not assumed available to rescue near-term liquidity. [S1,S9]

The counterfactual bear's ₹85.02 terminal price is NOT a floor, recovery value or downside estimate for actual EMA: it retains cash the real company spent. A credible actual downside price cannot be bounded from missing target claims; D remains NS. A temporary illiquid quote drawdown differs from permanent earnings impairment, but inability to exit can amplify both. Thesis-break variable: failure to reconcile positive, genuinely available post-deal funding together with target cash earnings after integration costs. Observable default, unauthorized fund diversion, or sustained negative owner cash generation would move the case beyond a research hold.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
Five-year price multiplication from ₹80 to ₹400/₹800 requires 37.97%/58.49% annual appreciation before dividends. Classification: Speculative / unsupported, not a quantified success probability. A full positive-earnings decomposition is unavailable because combined normalized owner earnings and current net claims are missing.

An explicit hurdle illustration avoids pretending revenue alone creates shareholder wealth. If all identified options are exercised, diluted shares are 24.224926 million and exercise cash ₹13.7031325 crore. At ₹400/₹800, required terminal common equity is ₹968.997/1,937.994 crore. With no other net cash/debt, a 10 x cash-EBITDA multiple and 20% margin, deducting option cash once requires revenue about ₹477.647/962.145 crore. Relative to management's unverified combined FY26₹195 crore, that is about 19.6%/37.6% five-year sales CAGR. At an 8 x multiple, the required revenue rises 25%, before any acquired debt or further dilution. [S1,S9,S10]

These are necessary arithmetic conditions, not a funded business forecast. Required consultant/RPO delivery capacity, client retention, margin convergence and financing are not established. Legacy post-pandemic revenue grew only 11.29% annually, while new units have lost money. The legacy counterfactual bull itself reaches about 4.40 x, and cannot be substituted for actual combined prospects. No supported multibagger designation is appropriate. [S1–S4]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Post-acquisition liquidity: reconcile March ₹108.367 crore gross treasury through actual buyback,₹96.751 crore deal, operating cash, taxes, capex, earmark releases, financing and target claims. Baseline current available cash ND. Warning: unexplained difference or reliance on restricted cash; thesis break: verified inability to meet due obligations. [S1,S5–S8]
2. Taggd economics: obtain audited profit/CFO, opening acquisition balance sheet and debt/claims. Baseline FY25 turnover ₹93.021 crore, FY26₹108 crore only management pro forma. Require cash profit after integration/retention costs, not revenue alone. [S7,S10]
3. Collections: baseline closing AR days 106.20, average 80.58, receivables ₹25.419 crore. Analyst warning: closing days above 120 without contractual explanation, rising one-year ageing, or no subsequent cash realization. Improvement below 90 would be useful, not sufficient alone. [S1]
4. Cash conversion: baseline five-year 64.96%, three-year 60.69%, FY26 CFO−₹0.660 crore. Seek positive next reporting-period CFO and conversion toward 80% over a meaningful rolling period; repeated sub 60% without temporary cause weakens CASH. [S1,S2,S4]
5. New-unit execution: compare April's promised twelve-month profitability with actual March 2027 results; baseline management new-business EBITDA loss about ₹11 crore and audited subsidiary losses. Continued material losses without cohort progress lower EXEC/CAP. [S1,S11]
6. IPO utilization: reconcile audited ₹22.968 crore remaining and March 2028 timeline, including ₹6.1934 crore acquisition eligibility. Track releases against actual eligible spend, not a second funding source. Unapproved diversion would be a governance trigger; a disclosed approved revision is not automatically diversion. [S1,S5]
7. Dilution and incentives: baseline 22.521426 million issued shares and 1.7035 million identified options. Review new grants, vesting, cancellations and issuance against cash returns per diluted share. A rescue issue materially below ₹80 would change the model. [S8,S9]
8. Governance/claims: verify promoter pledges, litigation disposition, audit KAM/qualifications, RPT pricing and the ₹0.76 crore contingency; no unsupported allegation is inferred while these remain open. [S1,S2]
9. Execution liquidity: retain 60-session median turnover ₹8.150 lakh, starting L3, plus lot-discrete final L1. Track eligible whole-lot days, bid depth and NSE caution categories. Outside ASM/GSM does not establish easy exit. [S12,S13,S20–S24]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Classification: Research Hold, acquisition/integration special situation. It is neither a demonstrated compounder nor an evidence-backed value purchase at ₹80. BQS/GQS/IAS are NS, so the numerical classification matrix cannot be forced. The compounder criteria fail evidentially: CAP/BAL are unresolved, GOV/MOAT/DUR are below 7 and CASH below 6. These observations do not imply the legacy business lacks value.

Action category: monitor and resolve information, not a portfolio recommendation or assumed position. A lower share price alone does not supply acquired earnings, available cash or senior claims. The apparent legacy P/E does not compensate for an unbounded perimeter gap. Reopen after audited target cash economics, reconciled funding, collection evidence and practical execution checks. If those are favorable, recalculate all 13 factors and a genuinely combined funded five-year valuation; do not import the counterfactual base price. If adverse evidence proves funding failure or governance abuse, apply the framework's explicit cap rather than retroactively treating today's unknown as known failure. [S1,S6–S12]

No ranking eligibility for any composite. This conclusion is price-dated and evidence-limited, not a permanent rejection or an insolvency prediction.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Source discipline: audited issuer filings anchor history; exchange files anchor quote, capital, liquidity and dated surveillance; management presentations/transcripts are labelled as such. Primary documents and calculation inputs are retained with exact URLs and page/row locators in the source and evidence ledgers. Reconstruction on 21 October does not admit later facts into the 20 October cutoff. The 19 October REG1 file's next-session 21 October applicability is explicitly prospective, not a post-cutoff observation. Current peer service pages supply only structural taxonomy, not dated financial/valuation claims.

Definitions: ₹crore=₹10 million. EBITDA excludes other income, depreciation and interest; normalized group PAT uses 25% tax on core pre-tax earnings; CFO/PAT uses sums and group PAT before NCI. Operating IC includes relevant goodwill, staff advances and deposits, excludes treasury and tax/interest assets, and uses average FY25/FY26 for ROIC. Closing and average receivable-day calculations are kept distinct. FCF proxy=CFO−cash operating capex, not automatically distributable owner cash. Gross treasury, restricted cash and transferable free cash are different measures.

Critical assumptions only in the legacy counterfactual: cash EBITDA margins and revenue paths,25% cash tax,2.8% D&A,3–4% capex, collection paths, stable operating asset/liability ratios, realizable group treasury, specified IPO releases, full contingency settlement,₹0.25 crore cost allowance, no new financing/dividends,5% revenue cash buffer,7 x/10 x/13 x terminal multiples and identified in-the-money option exercise. No target economics are invented. Actual transaction costs, taxes and cash-transfer frictions remain unknown and belong in the actual funding bridge once disclosed.

Open questions, prioritized: audited Taggd profit/CFO and acquisition balance sheet; acquired debt/senior/phantom settlement claims; dated current group and parent unrestricted cash; post-March operating/tax/capex/funding movements; eligible IPO-spending/reimbursement timing; subsequent receivable collections; consultant retention and organic price/volume/FX mix; current option register, pledges and litigation outcomes; executable bid depth and slippage. Absence of these inputs is not proof of wrongdoing. Verified legacy findings remain usable despite the total-company valuation hold.

score_note:
Nine business factors and four additional IAS factors, all on the framework's fixed integer scale:

GOV: 6/10; confidence medium; evidence E7, E8, E11, E12. Unmodified audit and disclosed RPTs/IPO allocation changes support adequate transparency; promoters did not sell into the buyback. Contrary evidence: loss-making deployments, subsequent large acquisition after a cash return, and missing post-deal economics prevent a stronger stewardship score. Ordinary litigation/RPTs are not evidence of diversion.

MOAT: 6/10; confidence medium; evidence E15, E3. Repeat business of 76.38% and high C-suite concentration evidence trusted relationships and specialized search capability. Contrary evidence: mandates are not annuities, consultants can leave, and global search/RPO competitors can contest accounts; no independently verified structural market-share moat.

REV: 7/10; confidence medium; evidence E2, E18. Five-year 22.2539% CAGR starts at 8; apply−1 for the pandemic-depressed FY21 base, corroborated by only 11.2876% FY22–26 growth. Three-year 20.3303% and H2FY26 recovery are positives, but not a second trajectory bonus. No small-size penalty or forecast/Taggd revenue bonus.

DUR: 6/10; confidence medium; evidence E15, E9, E19. Existing India/Dubai/Singapore relationships and acquired RPO clients create accessible adjacent demand; board advisory adds a plausible service avenue. Contrary evidence: hiring cyclicality, unproven cross-selling/unit economics, and loss-making new units mean headline TAM is not a funded runway.

CAP: NS/10; confidence low; evidence E13, E8, E9. Legacy operating ROIC is strong at 26.96%, but one-year incremental proxy is 4.27% and a ₹96.75 crore completed acquisition changes committed capital materially. Target profitability/acquired working capital/debt and new-unit cohorts are missing. No legacy ROIC substitution for current incremental returns.

CASH: 5/10; confidence medium; evidence E4, E5. Five-year 64.96% and three-year 60.69% reported conversion are mixed; FY26 negative CFO reflects collections and taxes, not capex. Contrary positive: FY24–25 CFO was positive and FY25 collection release helped. A one-year receivable spike is not enough to assert persistent destructive cash realization, so no≤3 override.

BAL: NS/10; confidence low; evidence E6, E8, E10, E12. Audited March debt was just ₹0.591 crore, a positive; however that cash predates buyback/acquisition and includes earmarked/group funds. Missing interim cash generation, target obligations and transferability prevent credible actual post-deal stress coverage. Conditional arithmetic gap is not proven default.

EXEC: 5/10; confidence medium; evidence E12, E18, E19. Taggd closure and completed buyback are delivered milestones, and H2 revenue recovered strongly. Contrary evidence: James Douglas losses, eroded-net-worth subsidiaries and abandoned Decision Dynamics plan; promised new-business profitability remains unverified. Do not score acquisition announcement as integration success.

EARN: 5/10; confidence medium; evidence E2, E3, E12. Recurring operating EBITDA grew 8%FY26 with revenue 18%, and normalized core group profit remains positive. Contrary evidence: ownerPAT belowFY24, dilutedEPS5.29 vs 8.40, investment income/deferred-tax credits and new-vertical losses weaken reported per-share growth quality.

R: NS/10; confidence low; evidence E9, E10, E17. Actual post-acquisition target earnings/claims and unrestricted liquidity are not established; no supported common-equity five-year base IRR. The fully funded no-Taggd counterfactual is not the purchased entity and cannot supply R, even though its base exceeds 15%.

D: NS/10; confidence low; evidence E10, E12, E17. Credible stress links recruitment slowdown, receivable stretch, target losses and restricted liquidity; March debt was low and legacy operations profitable. Actual target claims/funding gap are unknown, so downside severity/recovery cannot be scored from a counterfactual survival case.

P: NS/10; confidence low; evidence E3, E6, E9. 14.64 xFY26 ownerPAT and 20.22 xnormalizedlegacyPAT are only stale-perimeter references; they omit acquired target earnings and cash-yield loss. Current price-implied combined growth cannot be solved without a target earnings/claim bridge. Do not interpret the obsolete net-cash EV as a bargain.

L: 1/10; confidence high; evidence E1, E16, E20, E21. Starting L3 follows the lower of 60-session mean and median actual traded value, giving 12.27 continuous theoretical sessions. Whole-lot execution at 5% is much worse: only 10/60 dates eligible,13 total lots, and 27.69/32.31 mean-capacity sessions for six/seven lots. Apply an explicit two-point lot-size/execution downgrade to final L1. Positive contrary evidence: Active SM, no identified ASM/GSM/ESM measure and improved recent turnover. NSE liquidity cautions and unknown bid depth prevent an orderly-execution uplift.

BQS = 0.20 GOV + 0.20 MOAT + 0.12 REV + 0.10 DUR + 0.12 CAP + 0.10 CASH + 0.08 BAL + 0.08 EXEC. Known contributions are 1.20 + 1.20 + 0.84 + 0.60 + NS + 0.50 + NS + 0.40 = 4.74. Coverage 80%; raw and final NS. Missing-data bounds 4.94–6.74, not a confidence interval or substitute score.

GQS, Growth Quality Score, = 0.40 REV + 0.20 DUR + 0.15 EARN + 0.15 CAP + 0.10 CASH. Contributions: 2.80 + 1.20 + 0.75 + NS + 0.50 = 5.25. Coverage 85%; raw and final NS; missing-data bounds 5.40–6.75.

IAS = 0.25 final BQS + 0.35 R + 0.20 D + 0.10 P + 0.10 L. Only L contributes 0.10. Coverage 10%; raw and final NS; conservative missing-data bounds 1.00–9.10. BQS is not replaced with a midpoint or its known subtotal. All three scores are excluded from ranked lists.

No governance cap: GOV is 6 and G1 does not fail. No funding cap: G3 is unresolved, not an evidenced failure. No growth cap: CASH is 5 and persistent CAP≤3 has not been established. The framework would cap BQS/IAS at 3 after a substantiated governance failure, IAS at 3 after G3 failure, and GQS at 5 for persistent CAP/CASH≤3; those are contingent rules, not current findings.
